headline: Trust is the foundation of effective teams—without it, collaboration becomes expensive and slow
universal_truth: Trust is built in drops and lost in buckets; consistency over time creates reliability
fun_facts: High-trust teams outperform low-trust teams by up to 50% in studies
Trust activates oxytocin in the brain, which reduces stress and increases cooperation
It takes approximately 66 days of consistent behavior to form a habit of trust
discussion_questions: How do you know when you trust someone?
How do you rebuild trust after it's broken?

hook.script: Watch a team that trusts each other—they move fast, communicate effortlessly, take risks. Watch a team without trust—every decision requires checking, verifying, protecting. Trust is invisible infrastructure. Without it, everything slows down.

cliff.script: Trust seems like a feeling, but it's actually a prediction—a bet that someone will behave as expected. What creates this willingness to depend on others?

options.text: Trust builds through consistency over time—people doing what they said they'd do, repeatedly, until reliability is proven
options.response: Yes. Trust isn't given—it's earned through evidence. Each kept promise, each reliable action, adds to the trust account. Consistency is the currency.

options.text: Trust comes from liking someone and having good intentions
options.response: Good intentions help, but trust requires proof through actions...

fact1.title: Trust as Efficiency
fact1.script: Low-trust environments require contracts, oversight, verification—all expensive. High-trust environments move faster with less friction. Trust isn't just nice; it's economically essential. Organizations with high trust outperform by wide margins.

fact2.title: Vulnerability First
fact2.script: Research shows trust often starts with vulnerability—someone takes a risk first. Leaders who admit mistakes create trust faster than those who seem perfect. Showing trust can generate trust.

fact3.title: Asymmetric Building
fact3.script: Trust builds slowly and breaks quickly—built in drops, lost in buckets. One betrayal can destroy years of consistent behavior. This asymmetry means protecting trust is more important than building it.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Trust is built in drops and lost in buckets. Consistency over time creates reliability. Protect trust like the precious asset it is.

outro.script: That's Day 202. Tomorrow, we'll explore when people disagree—handling conflict. Until then, be consistent in one area where you want to build trust.

growTrack.title: Trust Deposit - Be Consistent
growTrack.activity: Identify one relationship where you want more trust. What consistent action could you take daily or weekly to build it? Trust is an account—make small deposits regularly. One kept promise at a time.
